title: Common laboratory apparatus
competency: Identify common laboratory tools and describe what each one is used for.

keywords.def: A place where science experiments are done.
The tools and apparatus used by students, teachers and scientists who work in a laboratory.
A tool or set of tools made for a task in the laboratory.
A tool for obtaining the mass of an object.
A glass container for holding liquids. It is also used to heat liquids.
A tool for carrying a hot beaker and removing the lid from a crucible.
A tube that holds small amounts of liquid for mixing or heating.
A shallow dish used for growing and counting bacteria.
A cylinder with a millilitre (ml) scale, used to measure volume. Also called a measuring cylinder.
A burner for heating things in the lab, with a flame you control.

en.text: Laboratory equipment is a set of tools for lab tasks. Each tool has a job. A triple-beam balance finds mass. A thermometer measures temperature. A Petri dish grows bacteria. Tongs carry hot things. Know your tools, and your lab work goes smoothly.

am.text: የቤተ ሙከራ መሣሪያዎች ለተለያዩ ሥራዎች የተሠሩ ናቸው። እያንዳንዱ መሣሪያ የራሱ ሥራ አለው። ሚዛን ክብደትን ይለካል። ቴርሞሜትር ሙቀትን ይለካል። ፔትሪ ሳህን ባክቴሪያ ለማሳደግ ያገለግላል። ወረንጦ ትኩስ ነገር ለመያዝ ያገለግላል።

screens.title: Tools in a kitchen
screens.text: Selam's mother bakes injera. She lifts the hot lid of the mitad with a cloth. A science lab has tools for jobs like this.
screens.ask: Which lab tool do you think carries hot things? Take a guess.
screens.after: Read Table 1 to check your guess.

screens.title: 1.2.1 Common laboratory apparatus
paras: Laboratory equipment is made up of different sets of apparatus.
They are designed for many tasks in the laboratory. Students, teachers and scientists use them.
You can work smoothly and efficiently only when you know the common apparatus. Some of it is shown in Table 1.

screens.title: Table 1 Laboratory tools and their use
paras: Each tool is made for its own job.
table: Obtaining the mass of an object
Holding liquids such as water (also used to heat liquids)
Transporting a hot beaker; removing the lid from a crucible
Holding small amounts of liquid for mixing or heating
Has a millilitre (ml) scale; used to measure volume
Heating the contents in the lab, with a flame that you control
screens.note: Correction: the printed Table 1 says a beaker is for "holding water". A beaker holds any liquid, not only water.

screens.title: Name the tools
defs: The tools and apparatus used by people who work in a laboratory.
A tool for obtaining the mass of an object.
A tool for carrying a hot beaker or lifting the lid off a crucible.
A dish for growing and counting bacteria.

screens.title: Find the mass
screens.text: You want to know the mass of a stone.
screens.why: A triple-beam balance obtains the mass of an object.
screens.clue: Which tool is for mass, not volume or temperature?

screens.title: Sort the tools
screens.text: What does each tool do? Put it in the right group.
items: It gives the flame for heating.
It holds small amounts of liquid.
screens.why: Each tool goes with its use in Table 1.
screens.clue: Look at the "Uses" column of Table 1 for each tool.

screens.title: Use of a Petri dish
screens.ask: A Petri dish is used for growing and counting ___.
screens.why: Table 1 says a Petri dish is for growing and counting bacteria.

screens.title: A hot beaker
screens.text: Abebe heated water in a beaker over a Bunsen burner. Now he must move the hot beaker to the bench.
screens.ask: What should he use, and why?
opts: Tongs, so his hands do not touch the hot glass
His bare hands, if he is quick
A Petri dish, to hold it
screens.ans: Tongs, so his hands do not touch the hot glass
screens.why: Tongs are used for transporting a hot beaker. Hot glass burns hands.
screens.clue: Read the use of tongs in Table 1.
screens.worked: Table 1 says tongs transport a hot beaker. So Abebe uses tongs and keeps his hands off the hot glass.

screens.title: Why learn the tools?
screens.ask: Why should you learn about the apparatus before you start an experiment?
opts: You can then skip the safety rules
You can work smoothly and efficiently only if you are familiar with it
screens.ans: You can work smoothly and efficiently only if you are familiar with it
screens.why: Familiarity with apparatus helps you work smoothly and safely.

en.text: A beaker holds any liquid, not only water. Its markings give only an approximate volume. When you need a more accurate volume, use a graduated cylinder. It has a millilitre scale. It is also called a measuring cylinder.

am.text: ቢከር ማንኛውንም ፈሳሽ ይይዛል፤ ውሃን ብቻ አይደለም። ምልክቶቹ ግምታዊ መጠን ብቻ ይሰጣሉ። ትክክለኛ መጠን ሲያስፈልግ የመለኪያ ሲሊንደር ተጠቀም። በሚሊሊትር የተመረቀ ነው።

screens.title: Exactly 50 ml
screens.text: Hana needs 50 ml of water for an experiment. She has a beaker with a few marks. She also has a tall, thin cylinder with many marks.
screens.ask: Which one do you think gives a more accurate 50 ml?
screens.after: Read the correction below to check.

screens.title: Correction: what a beaker does
paras: The printed Table 1 says a beaker is for "holding water".
A beaker holds any liquid, not only water.
Its markings give only approximate volumes.
Use a graduated cylinder when you need a more accurate volume. It is also called a measuring cylinder.
screens.note: This correction comes from the fact-checked source. The book's own table says only "holding water".

screens.title: The measuring tools
defs: A container that holds any liquid. Its marks give only approximate volumes.
A cylinder with a millilitre (ml) scale, for measuring volume. Also called a measuring cylinder.

screens.title: True or false?
screens.text: A beaker is only for holding water.
screens.why: A beaker holds any liquid, not only water.
screens.clue: Read the correction again. What can a beaker hold?

screens.title: Measure 50 ml
screens.text: You need about 50 ml of water for an experiment.
screens.why: It has a millilitre scale for measuring volume.
screens.clue: Which tool has a millilitre (ml) scale?

screens.title: Another name
screens.ask: A graduated cylinder is also called a ___ cylinder.
screens.why: The graduated cylinder is also called a measuring cylinder.
screens.clue: Its job is to measure volume.

screens.title: What does it measure?
screens.text: Match each tool to what it measures.
screens.why: These are the measuring tools in Table 1.
screens.clue: Look for the words mass, temperature and volume in Table 1.
screens.worked: Balance → mass. Thermometer → temperature. Graduated cylinder → volume (ml).

test.text: Which tool would you use to move a hot beaker?
test.why: Tongs are used to carry hot things.

test.text: A thermometer is used to measure the volume of a liquid.
test.why: A thermometer measures temperature. A graduated cylinder measures volume.

test.ask: A triple-beam balance is used to obtain the ___ of an object.
test.why: A triple-beam balance obtains the mass of an object.

notes.text: The printed Table 1 says a beaker is for "holding water". A beaker holds any liquid, not only water. Its markings give only approximate volumes, so use a graduated cylinder for a more accurate volume. The graduated cylinder is also called a measuring cylinder.
Both hooks (injera mitad lid; Hana measuring 50 ml) are added situations, marked "added": true.
